rationale: Correct ACES Delta's owner roster by removing the unsupported treatment of GIC, OTPP and AIMCo as direct owners. Those institutions, together with Manulife, invested as limited partners in Haddington ESP I. Current direct platform ownership is held through Chevron-controlled Magnum Development as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas as minority owner. Haddington's former indirect platform ownership ended when Chevron acquired Magnum in 2023; Haddington's separately managed ACES I construction equity remains project-level context rather than a direct ACES Delta platform ownership period.

companyFieldUpdates.name: ACES Delta, LLC
companyFieldUpdates.description: ACES Delta, LLC is a clean-hydrogen production and underground salt-cavern storage platform in Delta, Utah. The 2019 joint venture is currently owned by Chevron-controlled Magnum Development, LLC as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. as minority owner; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. Haddington Energy Partners III formerly owned the platform indirectly through Magnum and exited that position when Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum in 2023. Haddington ESP I separately manages construction equity in the ACES I project company, while GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife are investors in that fund rather than verified direct ACES Delta owners. The first stage comprises 220 MW of electrolysis and two salt caverns supporting more than 300 GWh of storage. All 40 electrolyzers were reported commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, with final start-up still expected later in 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

set.event: Magnum Development and Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems announced the Advanced Clean Energy Storage joint venture that became ACES Delta.
The U.S. Department of Energy closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee for the ACES I hydrogen-production and storage project; the facility is debt rather than equity ownership.

Haddington announced US$650 million of commitments to Haddington ESP I from GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife; the institutions invested as fund LPs, not as disclosed direct ACES Delta owners.
Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum Development from Haddington, obtaining a majority interest in ACES Delta; Mitsubishi Power Americas remained the minority joint-venture owner.
HydrogenPro reported that all 40 electrolyzers comprising the 220 MW first stage had been commissioned, while final project start-up remained expected in the second half of 2026.
